q: What are the chances that everybody who loss has less points than everyone who won?
short: This week it has essentially already happened: the lowest winner (your 1397) is above the highest loser (Commode Chokers, 1365), so the chance is close to 100% unless a stat correction swings 32 points.
answer:
Looking at Week 3 (Nov 2 to Nov 8), the five matchups are: Angel Reese 1762 beat WNBA Enjoyers 1325, Nifty Neighbas 1617 beat White Johnson 1288, Creamy Cropmen 1871 beat Shake and Blake 1249, Jacob's Globetrotters 1406 beat Trash pandas 1309, and Garebears 1397 beat The Commode Chokers 1365.

The winners scored 1762, 1617, 1871, 1406 and 1397. The losers scored 1325, 1288, 1249, 1309 and 1365. The lowest winner is you at 1397 and the highest loser is the Commode Chokers at 1365, so every loser scored less than every winner, with a 32 point gap.

The data shows no projected points left for any team this week (rest is 0 for all 10 teams) and it is nearly midnight Sunday, so the main thing that could break it is a late ESPN stat correction of 32 points or more, which is very unlikely. I would call it roughly 97 to 99 percent, with the remainder being the chance that Sunday's final scoring has not fully posted yet.

For context, this is not the norm. In Week 1 it did not hold: Creamy Cropmen won with 1196 while White Johnson lost with 1281. I did not check Week 2. Your own 1397 is the score holding it together, since it is the lowest winning score.
